findings.title: Mutations remain unguarded by `requirePermission` in several routers (including a governance state transition)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/governance.ts:184 — POST /change-requests/:id/submit now carries requirePermission("governance","edit"); approve/reject/implement/verify carry requirePermission("change-requests","manage") at :212/:245/:274/:303

apps/api/src/routes/client-onboarding-command-center.ts:136/:153/:176/:197/:244 — the five onboarding mutations now carry requirePermission create/edit/delete/edit (view on reads); fix commit 14a2b301 is an ancestor of HEAD
apps/api/src/middleware/permissions.ts:54-93 — requirePermission resolves per-org effective permissions and 403s without the module:action key; grep counts 209 call sites in apps/api/src/routes

apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:845 (task comments), :910/:947 (updates), :1196 (task approve), :1228 (portal-comment) — no requirePermission; file-level requireAuth+requireOrgAccess only (projects.ts:36-37)

apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:357 (reply-draft), routes/assets.ts:359 (comments), routes/findings.ts:456 (comments), routes/field-services.ts:266 (calculate) — mutations with only requireAuth+requireOrgAccess

findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: governance submit + all five client-onboarding mutations are now guarded (commit 14a2b301, ancestor of HEAD); residual unguarded mutations remain in projects/ai/assets/findings/field-services and the mount-level guard test does not cover permissions — partially-fixed.

findings.title: External integration syncs report success while dropping items, and `jsm-sync` has no HTTP retry
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/jsm-sync.ts:29-62 — PAGE_SIZE/MAX_PAGES constants and jsmFetch with 3 bounded retries on network errors, 429 and 5xx
apps/worker/src/tasks/jsm-sync.ts:114-134 — startAt pagination loop; :133 sets truncated at the page cap; :227-234 returns ok:false on truncation or any per-item error
apps/worker/src/__tests__/tasks/task-handlers.test.ts:106-160 — two-page sync asserts startAt=0/100 and success; a rejected first fetch retries and succeeds (fix commit 1a6a5712 / PR #150)
apps/worker/src/tasks/jira-sync.ts:206 — still returns { ok: true } although errors++ at :121 and :184; fetchJiraIssue retries only 429 (:62-66) and returns null for 5xx (:67)
apps/worker/src/tasks/stripe-reconcile.ts:146 — still returns { ok: true } although errors++ at :116 and :132; task is scheduled daily via apps/worker/src/schedule-config.ts:29-33
apps/worker/src/tasks/m365-calendar-sync.ts:115 — now returns ok:false when errors > 0 (reporting fixed there)
findings.impact: Daily Stripe reconciliation and on-demand Jira batch sync can partially fail while the task result says success, so the worker consumer and alerting treat dropped records as a clean run and staleness goes undetected.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the jsm-sync result contract in jira-sync and stripe-reconcile: return { ok: false, error } when errors > 0 (or a structured partial result); retry 5xx in fetchJiraIssue; add unit tests injecting a failing per-item write.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: jsm-sync pagination/retry/failure-reporting fix is present and tested (commit 1a6a5712, PR #150); jira-sync.ts:206 and stripe-reconcile.ts:146 still return ok:true after counting per-item errors — partially-fixed.

findings.title: Published error-handling contract contradicts the implementation (codes, 422, and `request_id`)
evidence: docs/API_ERROR_HANDLING.md:17-40 — documents the flat {success:false,error:{code,message,status,details?}} envelope and generic 5xx messages
docs/API_ERROR_HANDLING.md:42-67 — Zod failures are documented as 400 VALIDATION with details.issues and explicitly no 422
docs/API_ERROR_HANDLING.md:38-40 — request id is documented as the X-Request-ID header, not a body field

apps/api/src/middleware/error.ts:20-51 — AppError codes as-is, ZodError -> 400 VALIDATION, generic 5xx message; apps/api/src/types/index.ts:28-38 failure() shape; apps/api/src/middleware/request-id.ts:20-24 sets X-Request-ID

findings.title: SDK retries unsafe requests without an `Idempotency-Key` (duplicate creates on transient failure)
evidence: packages/sdk/src/client.ts:69 — unsafeMethods = POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; :176-178 — request() mints one Idempotency-Key per logical call, outside the retry loop
packages/sdk/src/client.ts:296 — postFormData also mints a single key for the whole call
packages/sdk/src/client.ts:83-140 — executeFetch retries retryable statuses/network errors with the same headers object, so the same key is reused across attempts
packages/sdk/src/__tests__/client-fetch.test.ts:99-118 — key sent on postFormData, absent on GET; :120-180 — regression test asserts the SAME key across three attempts of a POST
fix commit 08ad3d4d (API-P2-004; register cites #32) is an ancestor of HEAD
findings.impact: A transient 503 after commit no longer double-creates records: the API idempotency middleware replays the stored response for the reused key.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the same-key-across-retries regression test as new SDK methods are added.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the SDK sends a stable Idempotency-Key on unsafe requests (minted once per logical call) and the same key is asserted across retries (commit 08ad3d4d) — verified-fixed.

findings.title: Outbound webhook dispatcher uses a non-atomic idempotency check (duplicate deliveries under concurrency)
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:178-180 — per-endpoint claimIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey, "processing") before delivery; :185 sends Idempotency-Key; :230 releases the claim on failure
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:80-100 — same atomic claim + Idempotency-Key header; :190-192 releases the claim on transient failure

apps/api/src/__tests__/webhook-dispatcher-idempotency.test.ts:117-140 — three concurrent dispatches collapse to a single delivery and the persisted key matches the header; :142-160 — claim released on failure so a later retry proceeds
apps/worker/src/__tests__/webhook-dispatcher.test.ts:88+ — worker dispatcher idempotency coverage
fix commit d5e0d5b7 (WH-P1-001) is an ancestor of HEAD
findings.impact: Concurrent duplicate dispatches of one logical event collapse to one POST per endpoint in both the queue and inline paths.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the concurrency regression tests when the dispatcher is refactored.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both dispatchers use the atomic Redis SET NX claim (in-memory fallback) and release on failure, with concurrent-duplicate collapse covered by tests (commit d5e0d5b7, stranded remediation on main) — verified-fixed.

findings.title: Minor contract inconsistencies (`rateLimitByUser` non-enveloped 429, capped raw-array lists, no `request_id`)
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:27-40 — rateLimitByUser message is a plain string, so express-rate-limit sends a non-JSON 429 (the global limiter at app.ts:125-143 sends JSON with code RATE_LIMIT)

apps/api/src/middleware/csrf.ts:84-88 — 403 {error:{code:"CSRF_INVALID",message}} (no success:false, no status); middleware/idempotency.ts:30/:69-72 — 400/409 {error:"..."}; middleware/request-timeout.ts:7-12 — 408 {error:{code,message}}
docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md:44-55 — documents an enveloped RATE_LIMITED 429 that no limiter emits (per-user limiter sends text; global limiter uses RATE_LIMIT)

apps/api/src/lib/pagination.ts:28/:42/:52 — parsePagination/paginationMeta/applyPagination have zero call sites in apps/ or packages/; LIST_HARD_CAP (:19) raw arrays remain, e.g. routes/store/quotes.ts:192

findings.impact: Clients/SDK cannot parse limiter/CSRF/idempotency/timeout failures as the standard envelope (the SDK retries a non-JSON 429 as an opaque parse error), and docs still promise a JSON 429 that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Return failure("RATE_LIMIT", ..., 429) from all limiters, envelope CSRF/idempotency/timeout errors, align docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md, and either adopt or delete lib/pagination.ts while converting remaining raw capped arrays.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the X-Request-ID header is now emitted, but per-user 429, CSRF 403, idempotency 400/409 and timeout 408 are still non-enveloped, the rate-limiting doc still documents an enveloped 429, and the pagination helper is unused — partially-fixed.

findings.title: OpenAPI artifact is not bound to a commit and the CI audit warns (not fails) on documented-but-missing routes
evidence: scripts/openapi-audit.js:121-126 — exits 1 when statically-resolvable live routes are MISSING from the spec; :117-119 — EXTRA (dynamic/unresolved) entries are printed as warnings only
.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:29-34 — the audit runs in the shared unit-tests action used by test.yml and validate.yml
Faithful Python port of the audit at 8d299b8d: 440 statically parsed live routes, 0 MISSING, 257 dynamic/unresolved spec entries — gate PASSes (node is not installed in this audit shell)
docs/openapi.yaml:1-4 — generated header has no commit/date binding; :10 — static info.version "1.0.0"; artifact last regenerated at 1c1bd4ad
AGENTS.md:589 states "412 paths" while docs/openapi.yaml has 418 path keys and docs/INDEX.md:210 says 418; scripts/check-docs-counts.mjs:173-183 only checks docs/INDEX.md
findings.impact: The contract cannot be traced to the revision it represents, phantom spec entries can persist silently, and one committed doc count is already stale.
findings.recommendation: Embed the source commit (GIT_SHA) and generation date in docs/openapi.yaml; fail or allowlist EXTRA entries; update AGENTS.md:589 (and consider extending check-docs-counts.mjs to it).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the CI coverage gate now fails on missing routes and passes with 0 missing; commit binding, EXTRA allowlist and the stale AGENTS.md path count are still open — partially-fixed.

findings.title: Realtime client has no reconnect path; server emits `auth_expired` with no documented client handling
evidence: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:108-113 — es.onerror closes the EventSource and starts a one-shot 30s polling interval; it never reconnects the stream
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:115-118 — effect cleanup only closes the EventSource; the polling interval created in onerror is never cleared on unmount
grep auth_expired in apps/web → no listener anywhere (server emits it at apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:74-105 and ends the stream)
apps/api/src/__tests__/notifications-sse-scope.test.ts:16-38 — SSE org/user scope assertions exist (MT-P2-004), but no client reconnect test exists
findings.impact: After a token rotation, expiry or transient drop the bell degrades permanently to polling (up to 30s notification latency) until the component remounts, and the interval can leak after unmount.
findings.recommendation: Add an auth_expired listener (redirect to login) and bounded reconnect-with-backoff for onerror, close polling once reconnected, and clear the fallback interval in the effect cleanup; document the stream's disconnect contract.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the client is unchanged — no reconnect, no auth_expired handling, and the polling fallback is not cleaned up on unmount — still-open.

findings.title: Search falls through to an unscoped cross-tenant query
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:74-97 — requestedOrgId derives from req.orgScope; scoped org ids are applied via .in("organization_id", scopedOrgIds.length > 0 ? scopedOrgIds : ["__none__"]) so an empty scope fails closed
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:153-173 — the organizations query is org-scoped with the same fail-closed pattern
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts:136 (fails closed when the caller resolves to no organization), :214 (fails closed when a super admin's membership list is empty)
apps/api/src/lib/search.ts — sanitizeSearchTerm strips PostgREST operators (SEARCH-P1-001 regression tests in sanitize-search.test.ts)

findings.recommendation: None required; keep the fail-closed test as new search surfaces are added.

findings.title: OpenAPI schema is public and the Swagger UI is blocked by CSP
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/docs.ts:25-39 — docsDisabled() is NODE_ENV === "production", and both /openapi.json and /docs return 404 in production
apps/api/src/routes/docs.ts:1-20 — Swagger UI assets are SRI-pinned and the bootstrap script carries the CSP nonce
apps/api/src/__tests__/docs.test.ts:67-68 — asserts 404 for both routes in production

findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: routes/docs.ts 404s in production and the nonce/SRI wiring is covered by docs.test.ts — verified-fixed (ledger a97425d status carries).

findings.title: `/metrics` is fully public when `METRICS_TOKEN` is unset
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:154-171 — /metrics is gated by authorizeInternalRequest(req, getEnv().METRICS_TOKEN) and returns 404 when the token is unset or mismatched
apps/api/src/config/env.ts:63 — METRICS_TOKEN is an optional env key; deploy-do writes it and the Prometheus scrape uses a 0600 credentials file (PR #155/#166)
findings.impact: Metric labels are not exposed publicly; the endpoint is indistinguishable from a missing route without the token.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: /metrics is shared-token gated and 404s without METRICS_TOKEN — verified-fixed (ledger a97425d status carries).

findings.title: Batch Jira/JSM/M365 sync tasks are registered but never dispatched (no scheduler or enqueue path)
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/index.ts:35-37 — jira-sync, jsm-sync and m365-calendar-sync are registered
apps/worker/src/schedule-config.ts:57-60 — comment states they are intentionally NOT scheduled; apps/worker/src/__tests__/schedule-config.test.ts:39-41 asserts they are absent from scheduledScans

grep enqueueTask across apps/api and apps/web finds only webhook-dispatcher (apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:147), notification-email (apps/api/src/lib/notify.ts:215) and webhook-retry (apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:196) — no jira/jsm/m365 enqueue site exists
docs/JIRA_JSM_INTEGRATION.md:11,16 — the integration docs describe jira-sync/jsm-sync as "batch, periodic"
findings.impact: The batch reconciliation path (JSM ticket import, Jira task refresh, M365 reminders) never runs unattended; only real-time webhook status updates flow, and the docs promise periodic syncs that have no dispatch mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Either add a scheduled scan with explicit per-tenant payload (project/organization) or an admin-triggered enqueue endpoint/runbook, and correct docs/JIRA_JSM_INTEGRATION.md to match the chosen dispatch model.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.

findings.title: M365 calendar sync recreates a calendar event for every task on each run (duplicate events, no idempotency)
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/m365-calendar-sync.ts:79-112 — for every project task with due_at the handler POSTs a new event to /users/{upn}/events unconditionally
apps/worker/src/tasks/m365-calendar-sync.ts — no lookup of existing events, no stored Graph event id, no idempotency key or transactionId in the request body
apps/worker/src/tasks/m365-calendar-sync.ts:115 — errors are reported (ok:false), but a re-run after success duplicates every event
findings.impact: Repeated sync runs (manual enqueue today, any future schedule) create duplicate reminders for every task; there is no reconciliation path to detect or remove them.
findings.recommendation: Persist the created Graph event id per task and PATCH it on re-sync, or send a stable transactionId and reconcile existing events before creating; add a re-run test asserting no duplicates.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.

findings.title: M365 inbound webhook acknowledges but only processes the first notification of a batch
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:583-604 — every entry in event.value is validated for clientState (the SEC fix explicitly anticipates batched notifications)
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:612-644 — only const notification = value[0] is digested, deduped, audit-logged and metered; the remaining entries are dropped while the route returns success at :644
findings.impact: Batched Microsoft Graph change notifications after the first are acknowledged (so Graph will not retry) but never audited, deduped or metered — silent loss of integration events.
findings.recommendation: Iterate value[] and dedupe/audit each notification (aggregate the response), or explicitly document why only the first is processed; add a multi-notification test.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.

# API Contracts, Realtime, and Integrations Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8
- Repository: /tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target (MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech)
- Branch: main
- Commit SHA: 8d299b8d (merge PR #168; verified with `git log -1`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: subagent (prompt 08 pass, fresh read-only review + previous-register verification)
- Area code: API
- Output path: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/08_api_contracts_realtime_integrations.md
- Scope limitations:
  - Read-only static review at 8d299b8d. No runtime, database, Redis, Stripe/Jira/JSM/M365 or production access.
  - `node` is not installed in this audit shell, so `scripts/openapi-audit.js`, Jest suites and `tsx` scripts were **not executed**; the OpenAPI audit was reproduced by a faithful Python port (recorded below) and the rest is static analysis.
  - Worker handlers `module-tasks`, `scheduled-notifications`, `retention`, `orphan-cleanup` were skimmed, not exhaustively read; Next.js server actions were reviewed at surface level (they proxy the SDK).
  - This report covers the API lens; webhook replay/idempotency depth lives in domain 27, authz/tenancy in 06/24/25.

## Scope

Reviewed at HEAD `8d299b8d`:

- Routing/middleware: `apps/api/src/app.ts`, all 62 top-level + 13 subdirectory route files under `apps/api/src/routes/**` (61 mounted routers), middleware `auth.ts`, `permissions.ts`, `org-access.ts`, `admin.ts`, `idempotency.ts`, `optimistic-locking.ts`, `rate-limit.ts`, `csrf.ts`, `error.ts`, `not-found.ts`, `request-id.ts`, `request-timeout.ts`, `cache.ts`, `security.ts`, `security-headers.ts`.
- Contracts: `apps/api/src/openapi/spec.ts|builder.ts|generate.ts|extract.ts`, `docs/openapi.yaml`, `scripts/openapi-audit.js`, `.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml`, `scripts/check-docs-counts.mjs`, `docs/API_ERROR_HANDLING.md`, `docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md`, `docs/API_VERSIONING.md`, `docs/API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md`.
- SDK: `packages/sdk/src/client.ts` and the retry/idempotency tests.

- Webhooks/integrations: `apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts` (Stripe/Jira/JSM/M365 inbound), `routes/webhook-management.ts`, `lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts`, `lib/webhook-signature.ts`, `lib/ssrf-guard.ts`, `lib/pinned-fetch.ts`, worker `tasks/{webhook-dispatcher,webhook-retry,jira-sync,jsm-sync,m365-calendar-sync,stripe-reconcile}.ts`, `consumer-bullmq.ts`, `task-registry.ts`, `schedule-config.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/task-producer.ts`.

## Executive Summary

The API contract surface remains the strongest part of the platform, and the four reconciled P2 fixes are real at this commit: the SDK now sends a stable `Idempotency-Key` on unsafe requests (API-P2-004), both outbound webhook dispatchers claim deliveries atomically (API-P2-005), the published error contract matches the implementation (API-P2-003), and `jsm-sync` paginates, retries transient HTTP failures and fails the run on dropped records with tests (API-P2-002, jsm half). The OpenAPI coverage gate now fails CI on implemented-but-undocumented routes and passes with 0 missing.

What remains is boundary completeness and operational truthfulness, not headline architecture:

1. **Permission coverage is still uneven** (API-P2-001, partially-fixed): governance and client-onboarding are now guarded, but project comments/updates/task-approve, AI reply drafts, asset/finding comments and field-services calculations still run with auth + org access only, and the static route guard tests mounts, not permissions.
2. **Two of four integration syncs still lie about failure** (API-P2-002 residual): `jira-sync` and the daily `stripe-reconcile` return `ok:true` after counting per-item errors.
3. **Middleware error shapes bypass the envelope** (API-P3-001, partially-fixed): the per-user 429 is plain text, CSRF 403 / idempotency 400-409 / timeout 408 are hand-rolled, and `docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md` documents a JSON 429 that is never emitted.
4. **The generated contract is unbound** (API-P3-002, partially-fixed): `docs/openapi.yaml` records no commit, EXTRA spec entries only warn, and AGENTS.md still says 412 paths (actual 418).
5. **Realtime client resilience is unchanged** (API-P3-003, still-open): no reconnect, no `auth_expired` handling, polling interval leaks on unmount.
6. **New operational gaps**: the Jira/JSM/M365 batch syncs are registered but never dispatched despite docs calling them periodic; the M365 calendar sync duplicates events on every run; and the M365 inbound webhook drops every batched notification after the first.

Overall domain score: **4/5** — production-ready with tests/docs/observability, but not "continuously validated" because permission coverage, integration failure reporting and contract binding remain incomplete.

## Detailed Review

### Item: REST/RPC routes and validation

- Evidence: `app.ts:82-238`; 274 mutating registrations; `validators/*` (32 files); 209 `requirePermission` sites.
- What it does: All routers mount under `/api/v1`, mutate through Zod-validated handlers, and most module mutations pass through `requirePermission`. A static test (`route-authorization-guard.test.ts`) enforces auth/org mounts.
- Missing controls: Permission keys are not enforced by that test, and a residual set of mutations only has auth + org access (see API-P2-001). Public surfaces (`/analytics/track`, `/store/quotes`, `/public/submit`) are on the global IP limiter only.
- Risks: A view-only role can still write on the residual modules.

### Item: Error envelope and middleware errors

- Evidence: `types/index.ts:1-38`, `middleware/error.ts:20-51`, `middleware/not-found.ts`, `middleware/rate-limit.ts:27-40`, `middleware/csrf.ts:84-88`, `middleware/idempotency.ts:30/69-72`, `middleware/request-timeout.ts:7-12`.
- What it does: Thrown AppErrors and ZodErrors are normalized centrally; 5xx messages are genericized; 404s use the envelope; every response carries `X-Request-ID`.
- Missing controls: Errors produced by middleware (not the central handler) are not enveloped: per-user 429 is a plain string, CSRF 403, idempotency 400/409 and timeout 408 are ad-hoc `{error: ...}` shapes. `docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md:44-55` documents an enveloped `RATE_LIMITED` 429 that no limiter emits.
- Risks: The SDK's `res.json()` parse of a text 429 throws and is retried as an opaque error; clients cannot switch on a stable limiter code.

### Item: OpenAPI contract and CI gate

- Evidence: `openapi/spec.ts` (697 method entries), `generate.ts:1-60`, `docs/openapi.yaml` (418 paths, 16,588 lines), `scripts/openapi-audit.js:121-126`, `.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:29-34`.
- What it does: `buildSpec()` is served at runtime (404 in production) and materialized to `docs/openapi.yaml`; CI validates the spec and fails when a statically-resolvable route is missing. The ported audit at HEAD reports 440 live routes, 0 missing, 257 dynamic/unresolved entries — PASS.
- Missing controls: No commit/date binding in the generated artifact; EXTRA entries only warn; `AGENTS.md:589` still claims 412 paths; response schemas cover 14 routes and the error schema is not modeled.
- Risks: The artifact cannot be traced to a revision; phantom spec entries can persist; doc counts drift unchecked.

### Item: Idempotency (requests, webhooks, SDK)

- Evidence: `middleware/idempotency.ts:24-105`, `lib/idempotency.ts:99-185`, `routes/webhooks.ts:53-63/167-172`, `lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:140/178-180/230`, worker `tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:80-100`, `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:176-178/296`.
- What it does: Request keys are atomically claimed, owner+route scoped, replayed on success, released on failure; inbound webhooks dedupe on provider keys; outbound dispatchers claim per endpoint; the SDK now mints one key per logical unsafe call.
- Missing controls: The in-memory fallback is per-process (single instance today); `lib/idempotency.ts:9-18` mutex chain releases the next waiter before the critical section finishes, which is acceptable for tiny map operations but not a general mutex.
- Risks: Low in the current single-instance topology; the fallback weakens if scaled out.

### Item: Realtime SSE

- Evidence: `routes/notifications.ts:30-173`, `apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:81-119`, `__tests__/notifications-sse-scope.test.ts:16-38`.
- What it does: The stream authenticates via cookie/Bearer, re-validates the JWT every 5 minutes against all configured secrets, asserts user+org scope per row, sanitizes payloads, and sends keepalives; tests cover the scope assertion.
- Missing controls: The client closes the EventSource on any error and degrades to a one-shot 30s poll of the unread count only (no reconnect, no recent-list refresh), ignores the server's `auth_expired` event, and never clears the fallback interval on unmount; no disconnect/reconnect contract is documented.
- Risks: Up to 30s notification latency after any drop; interval leak; no user signal to re-authenticate.

### Item: External integrations and background delivery

- Evidence: worker `tasks/{jsm-sync,jira-sync,stripe-reconcile,m365-calendar-sync}.ts`, `schedule-config.ts:27-60`, `tasks/index.ts:35-37`, `lib/task-producer.ts`, `consumer-bullmq.ts`, `tasks/webhook-retry.ts`.
- What it does: Outbound HTTP has timeouts/retries/breaker; webhook delivery has a queue-first path with inline fallback, atomic dedup, retry task and DLQ; stripe-reconcile is scheduled daily; jsm-sync now paginates, retries and fails honestly.
- Missing controls: `jira-sync` and `stripe-reconcile` still return `ok:true` after per-item errors; `jira-sync` retries only 429 (not 5xx); jira/jsm/m365 syncs have no scheduler or enqueue path although docs describe them as periodic; M365 calendar sync duplicates events on re-run; the M365 webhook processes only the first batched notification; BullMQ failures land in the failed set with only logs (no queue DLQ/alert).
- Risks: Silent staleness in billing/Jira reconciliation; duplicate reminders; lost M365 events; dormant batch import.

### Item: SDK client

- Evidence: `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:20-140/149-303`, `__tests__/client-fetch.test.ts`.
- What it does: 30s timeout, 3 retries with exponential backoff on 429/502/503/504 and network/abort errors, stable `Idempotency-Key` on unsafe methods, CSRF and `X-Active-Org` headers, structured `ApiError`.
- Missing controls: `executeFetch` parses JSON before checking status, so a non-JSON 429 body throws a SyntaxError that is retried as a generic error; no runtime response validation.
- Risks: Opaque rate-limit errors; duplicate retries of a non-JSON 429.
